title: Product of Array Except Self
description:
For each position i, output the product of every element of the array except the one at position i. Do it without dividing: the array may contain zeros.

Input format
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n integers.

Output format
n integers on one line, separated by single spaces; the i-th is the product of all elements except a[i].
constraints: 2 <= n <= 15. -10 <= a[i] <= 10, so every product fits in a 64-bit signed integer.
hints: What would the answer be for position i if you only knew the product of everything to its left and everything to its right?
Build a prefix-product array (product of elements before i) and a suffix-product array (product of elements after i), then multiply them position by position.
Dividing the total product by a[i] breaks when a[i] is 0 (and loses the answer when there is exactly one zero). Use prefix * suffix instead.

examples.explanation: For index 0 the product of 2*3*4 is 24, and so on.
Only the position holding the single zero gets a non-zero product: (-1)*1*(-3) = 3.
